proposals.evidence: DEDR4616 explicitly gives Tamil makaḷ daughter, Malayalam mōḷ, Kota mōḷ, Kannada magaḷ, Tulu magaḷu, Parji māl and Gadaba māl. The selected survey makaḷ/magaḷ and shortened maka/maga/maha forms are comparative daughter extensions, with southern k/g/h variation and loss of final lateral; Parji/Gadaba māl/malu/melu preserve the separately documented central-Dravidian shape. Source gender/sense and vowel notation are retained; compounds and opaque contractions remain unassigned. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

Selected survey paḷam/payam/pagam/paśam/pām- responses preserve lect-specific reflexes or loss of the medial retroflex, and Kannada/related annu reflects loss of initial h-. These are comparative family proposals; the separate Indo-Aryan-looking phal forms and opaque responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4240 gives Tamil pukai, Malayalam puka, Kannada/Kodagu poge, Tulu pugè/pogè, Telugu poga and Gondi poya/poyo/poī smoke. Selected survey p-/h-/zero-initial and intervocalic k/g/h/y forms preserve that family; voga/voge have a glide onset following initial-consonant loss. Source vowel and consonant notation is retained, while opaque longer responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
